      "title": "Date override path returns available without checking busy times",
      "body": "checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist when it sees any override on the slot's UTC date and, if the slot is not rejected by the override conditions, returns true before the busy.every() check. As a result, any busy periods or accepted bookings for that user are ignored for slots covered by a date override, so users can be offered and potentially book slots that are already busy."

      "body": "The date override test uses dateOverrides.find and returns false when the slot is outside the iterated override. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the first override is outside the second, so find returns the second override and the slot is rejected. The correct condition is that the slot is inside at least one override, not outside any override."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 117,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override check allows slots that only partially overlap the override",
      "body": "The code treats a slot as outside an override only if slotEndTime is before or equal to the override start, or slotStartTime is after the override end. Therefore a slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is considered inside the override. For fixed-host round-robin availability this can expose slots when the fixed host is not available for the full event duration."
    },

      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",

      "title": "Working-hours check is inverted for multiple intervals and ignores event end time",
      "body": "checkIfIsAvailable uses workingHours.find and marks the slot unavailable if any working-hours entry reports the slot outside that entry. With multiple working-hour entries on the same day, a slot that is valid in one entry is outside another, so it is incorrectly rejected. Additionally, end is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so slots that start inside working hours but end after working hours pass. The check should determine that the full slot is contained in at least one working-hours interval."
    },

findings.title: Date override path returns available without checking busy times
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist when it sees any override on the slot's UTC date and, if the slot is not rejected by the override conditions, returns true before the busy.every() check. As a result, any busy periods or accepted bookings for that user are ignored for slots covered by a date override, so users can be offered and potentially book slots that are already busy.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides for the same day are handled as mutually exclusive
findings.body: The date override test uses dateOverrides.find and returns false when the slot is outside the iterated override. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the first override is outside the second, so find returns the second override and the slot is rejected. The correct condition is that the slot is inside at least one override, not outside any override.

findings.title: Date override check allows slots that only partially overlap the override
findings.body: The code treats a slot as outside an override only if slotEndTime is before or equal to the override start, or slotStartTime is after the override end. Therefore a slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is considered inside the override. For fixed-host round-robin availability this can expose slots when the fixed host is not available for the full event duration.

findings.title: Working-hours check is inverted for multiple intervals and ignores event end time
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable uses workingHours.find and marks the slot unavailable if any working-hours entry reports the slot outside that entry. With multiple working-hour entries on the same day, a slot that is valid in one entry is outside another, so it is incorrectly rejected. Additionally, end is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so slots that start inside working hours but end after working hours pass. The check should determine that the full slot is contained in at least one working-hours interval.

findings.title: Day.js objects are compared with ===
findings.body: The zero-length override check compares two Day.js objects with ===. This compares object identity and is always false for distinct Day.js instances, even if they represent the same instant. Use .isSame() if start and end equality is intended.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion assumes optional timeZone is present
findings.body: getSlots now reads override.timeZone to compute offsets, but TimeRange.timeZone is optional and no fallback is provided. If dateOverrides without timeZone are passed to getSlots, the offset calculation may use an unintended zone or fail depending on dayjs behavior. A fallback or required type should be used.

findings.title: Missing tests for the fixed-host round-robin override behavior
findings.body: The PR description says round-robin slots must respect fixed hosts' date overrides, but the added test only checks a personal event in another timezone. There is no regression test for round-robin with fixed hosts, multiple overrides, or busy times during a date override.

findings.title: Fixed hosts list recomputed for every slot
findings.body: Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for each slot. Since userAvailability does not change during the loop, this repeats work for every slot; compute fixedHosts once before filtering.
